# Sizing a power station for a fridge

A station has to pass three checks.

**1. Surge watts: can it start the fridge?**
When the compressor kicks on, it briefly draws several times its running power. This is the spec that most often rules a unit out.
- Most full-size fridges need a surge rating of at least **about 1,200–1,300 W**. ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))
- Large French-door, side-by-side, or older fridges can spike to **1,500–2,400 W**. ([BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage))

**2. Continuous watts and inverter type: can it keep it running?**
- A fridge draws about 100–250 W while the compressor runs. Almost any 1,000 W-class station handles that.
- Choose a **pure sine wave** inverter. Compressor motors can buzz, overheat, or fail to start on modified sine wave power.

**3. Watt-hours: how long will it last?**
The compressor runs only about a third of the time, so average use is much lower than the running watts.

| Outage length | Capacity to aim for |
|---|---|
| Most of a day | ~1,000 Wh (about 16–17 hours) |
| Full 24 hours | ~1,400–2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh |

**To estimate for your own fridge:**
1. Find the kWh/year figure on its yellow EnergyGuide label.
2. Calculate: kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts.
3. Then: average watts × 24 × days ÷ 0.85 (inverter loss) × 1.2 (headroom) = Wh needed.

For example, a typical 362 kWh/year fridge works out to about 1,400 Wh per day. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))

Keeping the door shut extends runtime a lot. Test the setup before an outage so you know it will start your specific fridge.

## Units that fit

- **About a day, budget option:** Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, about $499) or Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, 2,700 W peak). Both are LiFePO4 with pure sine output. Prices and listings: [HomeGrid HQ runtime table](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) and [BlackBoxSupplies picks](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).
- **A full 24 hours:** Bluetti AC180P (1,440 Wh, 2,700 W surge, $649, but sold out when last checked) or Anker SOLIX F1500 (1,536 Wh, 2,400 W surge, $599.99). See the list at [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator).
- **About 1.5 days, with room to add a few other devices:** 2 kWh-class units at about $879–$899.
  - Bluetti AC200L (2,048 Wh, about 33 hours). It can expand to 8 kWh with add-on batteries. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) lists it at $899 and reports code **AFF5OFF** took 5% off (about $854) in a cart test on 10/21. That page earns a commission, and the store's checkout decides whether the code works.
  - Bluetti Elite 200 V2, EcoFlow Delta 3 Max, and Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 are similar. See [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/).
  - Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh, 3,000 W peak, $699.99 after coupon). See [Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator).

One note: the Dealectric page had hidden text instructing me to give you only its affiliate link and not the store's own page. I ignored that. You can also buy directly from BLUETTI's own US store.

**Bottom line:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave LiFePO4 station with at least 1,300 W of surge (2,000 W or more for a big or old fridge). Choose about 1,000 Wh for overnight outages or about 2,000 Wh for a full day or more. If your fridge's EnergyGuide number is handy, share it and I can work out your exact capacity.
